reconcile.connective: Defenders read the Chronicles list as ordered by dynastic importance, not birth: Solomon is the eldest of the four but named last because the royal line runs through him.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells of The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who notes that 2 Samuel makes Solomon the replacement child born straight after the first son's death, while 1 Chronicles 3:5 lists him fourth of four.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Solomon David's second or fourth son by Bathsheba?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/solomon.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; print ed. 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Solomon is mentioned last, though he was the eldest of these four sons, because the genealogy was to be continued from him.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the second-vs-fourth ordering tension: explains Solomon is listed last in 1 Chr 3:5 not because he was youngest but because he was the eldest and the line is continued from him.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Of course Solomon was not her "only son," but he is called so (Pro 4:3) from the distinguished affection of which he was the object; and though the oldest, he is named the last of Bath-sheba's children.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Second distinct voice on the same ordering point: Solomon though the oldest of Bathsheba's sons is named last in the Chronicles list, so the order is not chronological.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), on 1 Chronicles 3:5
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, resolving the order: Solomon, though the eldest of the four sons, is listed last because the genealogy is continued from him.
